drivers.source: Actuals from Broadcom's quarterly releases (8-K Ex.99.1, source ids 60-66): Q1 FY25 $4.1B, Q2 'over $4.4B', Q3 $5.2B, Q1 FY26 $8.4B, Q2 FY26 $10.8B, Q3 FY26 $16.7B; Q4 FY25 6,460 derived from the Q3 FY26 release (Q4 FY26 guide $21.7B 'up 236% year-over-year' -> 21.7 / 3.36 = 6.46, id 66). Q4 FY26: TPU units (UBS, Morgan Stanley, Epoch: src 121, 122, 123; src 121 cleared by a none-newer search 2026-11-18) x revenue per unit; FY2027/FY2028: customer GW x $/GW (inputs_detail rows 'AI revenue per GW', 'FY2027 AI revenue', 'FY2028 * GW realised', source ids 37, 38, 47, 48).
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY26 21,496 built from units x revenue per unit (rebuild 2026-11-09, networking rebuilt 2026-11-17; was 22,177 = guide x the median beat). Units (estimate): Broadcom TPUs CY2026 ~3.215M = the set's average of UBS's 3.68M Broadcom TPUs for 2026 [src 121] and Morgan Stanley's 3.2M TPUs in 2026 [src 122] less MediaTek's 0.45M [src 121] (reading Morgan Stanley's figure as the all-designer total is the set's inference): (3.68 + 2.75) / 2 = 3.215M. Jan-Jul ~1.429M from Epoch (Q3 FY26 ~800k, up ~65% q/q, so Q2 ~485k; Q1 ~433k at the middle of the +2% to +22% quarterly range, one third of it in January = 144k [src 123]); the remaining 1.786M over Aug-Dec, rising evenly from a ~300k July month, gives Aug-Oct ~1.014M (319k + 338k + 357k). XPU revenue per unit $15.56k (estimate) = Q3 FY26 $15.24k (XPU revenue 16,700 x 0.73 = 12,191 / ~800k units) + $0.32k more HBM as TPU 8i (288 GB vs Ironwood's ~192 GB [src 126]) ramps to a quarter of units: 96 GB x ~$12.2/GB HBM3e [src 127] x 0.25 x 1.1 (memory resold at ~10%, judgment). Q3 FY26 call: Broadcom to 'ramp up high-volume shipments of the TPU version 8i to Google' and 'accelerate shipments of Ironwood to Anthropic' (ids 37, 38). XPU 1,014k x $15.56k = 15,778. AI networking from the compute it connects (rebuild 2026-11-17, carry-forward fix; was Q3 FY26's filed ratio to all XPU revenue, 5,836): Q3 FY26 networking 4,509 = 16,700 x (1 - 0.73) (Q3 FY26 call: XPUs 'represented 73% of AI revenue', ids 37, 38) = 0.445 x the non-HBM part of XPU revenue 12,191 x (1 - 16.9%); Q4 HBM is 18.6% of XPU revenue as TPU 8i ramps. drivers.label: Custom XPU share of AI semiconductor revenue (rest = AI networking)
drivers.source: Calls: Q1 FY26 'AI networking ... represented one third of total AI revenue' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/03/04/broadcom-avgo-q1-2026-earnings-call-transcript); Q2 FY26 'Networking represented almost 40% of our Q2 AI revenue' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/03/broadcom-avgo-q2-2026-earnings-transcript/); Q3 FY26 XPUs 'represented 73% of AI revenue' (ids 37, 38). Outlook: Q2 FY26 call, networking share 'closer to around 30%' and 40% 'probably as high as' it goes; Q3 FY26 call, networking 'expected to grow just as fast as XPUs over the next few years'; Q4 FY26 'both XPUs and AI networking revenue to triple year on year'. (Q1 FY26 id 87; Q2 FY26 id 88) Q4 FY25 call (id 77): of the $73B AI backlog 'maybe $20 billion of it is everything else. The rest, is XPUs.'
drivers.derivation: Actuals FY26: 0.667 / 0.61 / 0.73 (cited). FY25 quarters 0.65: not read from the FY25 calls (base year only; feeds no forecast and no filed-quarter EBIT). Q4 FY26 0.734 (rebuild 2026-11-17; was 0.73 at Q3 FY26's filed ratio, and 0.663 from the Q4 'both triple' outlook before 2026-11-09): XPU 15,778 / AI 21,496, networking tied to non-HBM XPU content as for FY27-29 below. FY27-FY29 rebuilt 2026-11-17 (carry-forward fix; the 0.73 for every quarter repeated the last filed split): networking is built from the compute it connects, XPU revenue from compute plus the HBM Broadcom resells inside it. Q3 FY26: networking 4,509 (16,700 x 0.27) = 0.370 x XPU revenue 12,191 (16,700 x 0.73; the call's 'represented 73% of AI revenue', ids 37, 38), and HBM was ~16.9% of XPU revenue (the set's estimate in the xpu_margin build: Ironwood's ~192 GB from Tom's Hardware, src 126, x the HBM3e price ~$12.2/GB from Silicon Analysts, src 127, x 1.1, over the set's $15.24k XPU revenue per unit; neither page gives an HBM share), so networking = 0.445 x the non-HBM part of XPU revenue (0.370 / 0.831). Switch, scale-up and optics ports scale with compute dies and cluster size, not with memory GB, and the Q3 FY26 call ties the networking outlook to XPU deployments ('expected to grow just as fast as XPUs over the next few years'; Tomahawk 6 and Tomahawk Ultra 'deployed in pretty much all of the AI hyperscalers that are building XPUs with us', ids 37, 38), while the CFO names 'the increasing mix of XPUs with their increasing memory content' (id 38). HBM share of XPU revenue by year from the set's own xpu_margin build: FY27 23.4% (TPU 8i, 288 GB, every XPU), FY28 31.5% (TPU revenue share 0.675, half of it on TPU v9 at 47.5% HBM per owner card 2026-11-16 'v9 HBM4, half of FY28', rest 23.4%), FY29 39.5% (TPU 0.669 all v9, non-TPU 23.4%). XPU share = 1 / (1 + 0.445 x (1 - HBM share)): FY27 0.7457, FY28 0.7664, FY29 0.7879, the same each quarter of a year (the HBM shares are yearly, as in xpu_margin). Reading 'grow just as fast' as revenue would keep the share at Q3 FY26's 0.73; that, the Q2 FY26 call's networking 'closer to around 30%' (0.70, id 88) and the HBM step on TPUs only are sized as alternatives. Moderately conservative: a higher XPU share lowers the AI margin (networking ~72% vs XPUs 46-56%). Not changed here: the FY27 Google TPU line in ai_rev, grossed up for networking at 0.73 (25,000 / 0.73), which at the rebuilt 0.7457 would be 25,000 / 0.7457; sized as an ai_rev alternative. | SemiAnalysis cut: owner pick 2026-11-17 (Owner card 2026-11-17 9:38 AM ET (cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLHb22faGDqKhees5ZNgh1HH) 'Volume net of moratorium') books it as volume on ai_rev, so this driver stays on its 11-16 path.
drivers.why: Mix lever: networking earns ~72% and XPUs ~52-59%, so each point of share moves the AI margin by ~0.2pt.
drivers.variant: Upside mix: 0.73 kept (Q3 FY26 split, 'grow just as fast as XPUs' read as revenue, ids 37, 38) or 0.70 (Q2 FY26 call: networking 'closer to around 30%', id 88); downside: higher still if rack-level systems are booked in the XPU line (no source shows this yet).

drivers.label: Custom XPU operating margin (non-GAAP, before SBC)
drivers.source: Not disclosed. Actual quarters = derived AI margin (Semiconductor solutions operating income less non-AI x 52.5%, id 68; non-AI margin row 'constant: nonai_margin') less networking share x 72%, over XPU share. Qualitative: CFO Q2 FY26 'our ASICs, TPUs ... lower margins' and 'the AI networking side ... has very rich margins'; Q3 FY26 'increasing mix of XPUs with their increasing memory content ... diluting our consolidated gross margin' (ids 37, 38). Analyst view only: racks 'maybe 45%-50% gross margin' (UBS's Arcuri on the Q1 FY26 call, id 87; not a company figure).
drivers.derivation: FY26 derived 57.6% / 59.7% / 59.5% (segment operating income 7,503 / 9,281 / 12,770 less non-AI x 55% less networking x 72%, over XPU revenue; re-derived 2026-11-09 for the rebuilt non-AI margin, was 59.4% / 61.3% / 60.3% at 52.5%). Q4 FY26 58.75% (rebuild 2026-11-09; was 58.6%, taken from the Q4 operating-margin guide): Q3 FY26 filed-derived 59.45% less ~1.0pt as HBM rises from ~16.9% to ~18.6% of XPU revenue (HBM shares are the set's estimate, not on any page: Tom's Hardware gives only the capacities, TPU 8i 288 GB vs Ironwood ~192 GB [src 126], and Silicon Analysts the HBM3E 2026 price ~$12.2/GB [src 127]; neither page gives an HBM share or a margin. Q3: 192 GB x $12.2 x 1.1 = $2.58k of $15.24k per unit = 16.9%; Q4: +$0.32k = $2.90k of $15.56k = 18.6%. Memory resold at ~10% margin (judgment) vs ~69.5% on the rest, the split that gives Q3's filed-derived margin: (59.45% - 16.9% x 10%) / 83.1% = 69.5%; step 1.7pt x (69.5% - 10%) = -1.0pt; CFO: 'the increasing mix of XPUs with their increasing memory content ... is diluting our consolidated gross margin', ids 37, 38), plus ~0.3pt as semiconductor opex ($1.2B in Q3, 'OpEx representing 6% of segment revenue') spreads over more revenue. FY27-FY29 rebuilt 2026-11-16 (thread 'Source AVGO TPU margin and FY29 AI revenue'; was 58.75% held, owner card 2026-11-09 'Hold both flat' was on the UBS rack-margin question; gate 2026-11-16 failed the hold as unsupported): 55.90% for every XPU. TPUs: the Q3 FY26 call transcript (id 38, re-opened 2026-11-18) says 'Broadcom is now shipping the TPU version 8i ahead of the MediaTek version v8t', 'ramp up high-volume shipments of the TPU version 8i to Google' and 'We expect Anthropic to deploy another 5 gigawatts of TPU version 8i in 2027', so Broadcom's 2027 TPU units are 8i. Memory per chip (288 GB) is from Tom's Hardware (src 126; the page has no margin or HBM-share figure; Tom's Hardware and other press name MediaTek for 8i and Broadcom for 8t instead, sized below). The set's formula: HBM 288 GB x $12.2/GB (src 127, HBM3E 2026 per-stack blend) x 1.1 = $3.87k of $16.53k per unit = 23.4% of revenue; 76.6% x 69.5% + 23.4% x 10% + 0.3pt opex leverage = 55.90%. Non-TPU XPUs (OpenAI Jalapeno, Meta MTIA): no source gives their HBM content (searched 2026-11-16); the CFO's 'increasing mix of XPUs with their increasing memory content ... diluting our consolidated gross margin' (Q3 FY26, id 38) is about XPUs generally, so they take the same HBM share (the conservative reading; the 58.75% hold is sized as an alternative). FY28-FY29 add the TPU v9 HBM step (owner card 2026-11-16 12:47Z 'v9 HBM4, half of FY28'): JPMorgan via relay (src 144) has v9 ramping in volume in 2028 with four compute dies and 16 HBM stacks; build = 16 x 36 GB HBM4 12-hi stacks = 576 GB x $36.11/GB (Silicon Analysts, CY2027 supply expected, src 127) x 1.1 = $22.88k per chip on non-HBM value 2x 8i's $12.66k (four compute dies; the set's estimate) -> HBM 47.5% of TPU revenue, TPU margin 41.6%; v9 on half of FY28 TPU revenue (ramp year) and all of FY29, TPU revenue shares from the ai_rev rows (FY28 0.675, FY29 0.669), non-TPU and 8i units at 55.90% -> FY28 51.06%, FY29 46.30%. Caveat: revenue per GW stays $11.5B, so HBM4 cost passed through is not added to revenue. CEO Hock Tan cross-check: 'sustain operating margin even as mix of products dilutes the gross margin' (consolidated, id 38). | SemiAnalysis cut: owner pick 2026-11-17 (Owner card 2026-11-17 9:38 AM ET (cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLHb22faGDqKhees5ZNgh1HH) 'Volume net of moratorium') books it as volume on ai_rev, so this driver stays on its 11-16 path.
drivers.why: Sets the XPU profit pool; the rack mix lands here.
drivers.variant: Downside: racks 50% of XPU revenue by FY28 (XPU ~50.4%); upside: racks capped at 20% (XPU ~55.4%).

drivers.label: Infrastructure software revenue (VMware and mainframe/enterprise software)
drivers.source: Actuals = Infrastructure software segment revenue (id 68). Q4 FY26: Q3 FY26 call (ids 37, 38): 'We expect Q4 infrastructure software revenue of approximately $8.7 billion' (declared guide use, guidance_check 'infrastructure software revenue' Q4 FY2026); 'we sustained ARR growth of 15% year-on-year'. Gartner via The Register (https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/11/gartner_vmware_migration_advice/); CloudBolt via Petri (https://petri.com/vmware-pricing-fears-enterprise-virtualization-shift/).
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY26 8,700: the company figure, 'We expect Q4 infrastructure software revenue of approximately $8.7 billion' (Q3 FY26 call, ids 37, 38), used as a declared last resort (guidance_check row 'infrastructure software revenue' Q4 FY2026, guide_use): Broadcom gives no VMware renewal calendar, and recognized software revenue does not track the one disclosed driver, ARR (Q3 FY26 revenue 8,752 was +29% y/y against ARR +15%), so no driver build sets one quarter. Its FY26 record: Q1 FY26 guide ~$6.8B vs 6,796 (-0.06%), Q2 FY26 guide ~$7.2B vs 7,178 (-0.3%), Q3 FY26 guide ~$8.9B vs 8,752 (-1.7%); the guide x the Q2-Q3 FY26 average miss (8,614) is sized as an alternative. Was 8,750 (gate 2026-11-17: the guide booked without a declaration). FY27-FY29 rebuilt 2026-11-17 (carry-forward fix): revenue follows VMware's recurring base, which is the installed workloads times the price per workload. (1) Today: ARR +15% y/y at Q3 FY26 ('we sustained ARR growth of 15% year-on-year', id 38; +17% at Q2 FY26, id 88) and management expected the faster VMware growth 'to continue' (Q2 FY26 call, June 2026, id 88). That growth is the first Broadcom-era repricing onto VCF: in CloudBolt's January 2026 survey 14% of customers saw increases above 100%, 12% 50-99%, 33% 24-49% and 31% below 25% (via Petri, https://petri.com/vmware-pricing-fears-enterprise-virtualization-shift/). (2) Workloads: Gartner expects 'More than a third of workloads currently running under VMware will run on another platform by 2028' (The Register, 2025-09-11, https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/11/gartner_vmware_migration_advice/): 35% lost over Sep 2025-Dec 2028 = -12.4% a year; CloudBolt: '86% of organizations report actively reducing their VMware footprint'. (3) Once the first repricing has passed through the base, growth = renewal share x renewal uplift less attrition: a third of the base renews each year (three-year VCF subscriptions; estimate) at +24%, the bottom of the survey's median bucket (24-49%) as a second-cycle uplift (judgment, moderately conservative), so (1 + 0.24 / 3) x (1 - 12.4%) - 1 = -5.4% a year. Path: ARR growth fades from +15% (Q3 FY26) to -5.4% by Q4 FY27 in even steps (+9.9%, +4.8%, -0.3%, -5.4% annualised in Q1-Q4 FY27; 'multiple quarters' from June 2026), then -5.4% a year in FY28; each quarter = the one before x (1 + annual rate)^(1/4). FY29 (Nov 2028-Oct 2029) runs past Gartner's 'by 2028' window, so no source covers it: the -5.4% a year there is judgment (moderately conservative: attrition is assumed to go on at Gartner's pace for one more year); attrition ending (+8% a year, renewal uplift only) and a flat FY29 are sized as alternatives. FY27 35,807.6, FY28 34,317.2, FY29 32,461.4. Alternatives sized: flat at 8,700 ('approximately $8.7 billion'), ARR +15% a year, no second-cycle uplift, uplift at the median bucket's middle (36%), Q4 at the guide x the median miss, FY29 attrition ending. Margin: constant sw_margin (94% gross margin less a judgment $919M opex a quarter).
drivers.why: ~25% of FY26 revenue at ~84% margin; the stable earnings floor.

drivers.label: Customer-financing exposure backed by Broadcom (probability-weighted, utilised)
drivers.source: 10-Q 2026-08-02 R17/R54: Backstop max ~$29B, $42B convertible-note facility (ids 29, 31); 8-K Item 2.03 2026-10-27: SPV Backstop max ~$43B (id 67); OpenAI >$50B package (WSJ, id 45); XPV aims '>20 gigawatts ... by the end of 2028' (ids 37, 38).
drivers.derivation: Each deal at its maximum x 70% average utilisation x probability Broadcom carries it: 10-Q Backstop 29,000 x 0.7 = 20,300 and Anthropic senior notes 42,000 x 0.7 = 29,400 (Q3 FY26, 49,700); Oct 27 SPV Backstop 43,000 x 0.7 = 30,100 (Q4 FY26, 79,800); OpenAI 35,000 x p 0.6 x 0.7 = 14,700 (from Q2 FY27, 94,500); future XPV backstops 32,000 x p 0.5 x 0.7 = 11,200 (from Q2 FY28, 105,700). The loss uses the FY28 year-end stock (every deal expected by 2028). FY2029 rebuilt 2026-11-17 (carry-forward fix; was the FY28 stock 105,700 in every quarter): the backstops fall as the leases are paid. The Oct 27 8-K says the Backstop maximum is reached on deployment and the liability is 'rising with deliveries and falling with lease payments' (id 67); the 10-Q Backstop covers 5-year leases (ids 29, 31). Each deal's FY28 stock is run forward by its remaining rent: cohorts amortise straight-line over 5 years from lease start, so remaining(t) = sum of each cohort's 1 - (t - start) / 5, and FY29 = FY28 stock x remaining(t) / remaining(FY28 end). Lease starts (estimate): 10-Q Backstop evenly over Q1-Q2 FY27 (the $35B tranche closed June 2026 for Anthropic's 1 GW; Reuters on the prospectus: expanded TPU access 'beginning in 2027', src 141); Oct 27 SPV over FY27 on the FY24-26 quarter shape (Anthropic's 5 GW of TPU 8i in 2027, id 38); OpenAI package over Q2 FY27-Q4 FY28 by the set's GW (1.3 FY27, 3.5 FY28); future XPV over Q2-Q4 FY28 (XPV 'by the end of 2028', ids 37, 38). Anthropic notes 29,400: no repayment in FY29, as the 10-Q gives no maturity or amortisation for the notes and they fund the lease rent (id 29). No new Broadcom-backed deal in FY29: no source names one (the OpenAI 10 GW deal runs to end-2029, src 142, but the WSJ package, id 45, is the only financing reported; financing for FY29's 3.64 GW at the FY27-28 ratio is sized as an alternative). Q4 FY29 by deal: 10-Q Backstop 14087, SPV 21694, OpenAI 11310, XPV 8805, notes 29,400. FY29 quarters 100,599 / 95,498 / 90,397 / 85,296. Caveat: the liability is the covered share of rent owed less the racks' resale value, so it falls with rent only if rack value falls in step (judgment). Value-neutral: the expected-loss adjustment reads the FY28 stock (cf_exposure_y3).
drivers.why: Replaces the fixed -4,568 adjustment: loss = exposure x loss rate.

drivers.label: Lifetime expected loss rate on Broadcom-backed customer financing
drivers.source: S&P 1981-2024 five-year cumulative defaults BB 5.05%, B 14.69% (id 49); Anthropic junior 10% coupon vs ~7% BB index (id 50); deal rows in inputs_detail (PD Anthropic 10.5%, OpenAI 16.75%, mixed 12.5%; LGD 35-45%).
drivers.derivation: Exposure-weighted PD x LGD of the five deals: 10-Q Backstop 10.5% x 45% (959), Anthropic notes 10.5% x 35% (1,080), Oct 27 SPV 10.5% x 35% (1,106), OpenAI 16.75% x 35% (862), future XPV 12.5% x 40% (560): 4,567.6 / 105,700 = 4.3210%. Unconditional (the downside revenue loss sits in the downside case, not here). FY2029 unchanged.
drivers.why: With cf_exposure sets the equity-level customer-financing loss.
drivers.variant: Tail stress (both labs default, racks ~30% of cost): ~33% loss rate, ~$35B.

drivers.label: Optics share of AI networking revenue (optical DSPs + EML/CW/VCSEL lasers + CPO)
drivers.source: Not disclosed by Broadcom. Company: CEO Hock Tan, Q3 FY26 call: 'leader in leading-edge optical DSPs', 'leader in EMLs, VCSELs, and CW lasers' with 'a fairly substantial share'; Charlie Kawwas (President, Semiconductor Solutions Group): laser/InP fabs 'more than tripling' y/y (id 76); CEO Hock Tan, Q4 FY25 call: lasers 'relatively lesser dollars' than XPUs, ~$20B of the $73B AI backlog is switches + DSPs + lasers (id 77). Market: AI optical transceivers ~$16.5B in 2025 (TrendForce via Aetrix, id 78); LightCounting 2026-10-08: Ethernet optical transceiver sales +120% in 2026, +76% in 2027 (src 162); TrendForce 2026-11-02: pluggable transceivers $84.1B in 2027, +76% (src 161); DSP 20-40% of an 800G BOM (id 79); Marvell 60-65% of 'one key type' of the signal-processing chips it sells to optical module makers (Stifel via TheStreet, id 80; the page does not name the type: reading it as optical DSPs, the Broadcom/Marvell duopoly of id 81, is the set's inference), a Broadcom/Marvell duopoly (id 81); 1.6T chipsets >$2B in 2026 (LightCounting, id 84); Lumentum 50-60% of EMLs (id 83), Lumentum+Broadcom+Mitsubishi ~72% of EMLs, Broadcom a CW-DFB leader (TrendForce, id 78); Lumentum Components revenue $443.7M / $533.3M / $649.4M / $754.2M in its quarters ended Dec 2025 - Sep 2026 (Lumentum 8-Ks, src 164, src 163).
drivers.derivation: Rebuilt 2026-11-18 (carry trace: Q4 FY26 0.1135 was the base round's value while the text quoting it had moved to the rebuilt networking). FY26 Broadcom optics ~$2.49B = optical DSPs ~$1.91B + lasers ~$0.58B + CPO ~0 (pre-volume). DSPs: 2026 AI optical transceiver market $36.3B = 2025 $16.5B (TrendForce, id 78) x 2.2 (LightCounting's +120% for 2026, src 162); x 0.70 BOM/price (judgment: module makers' ~30% gross margin) x 0.25 (low-middle of 20-40%, id 79) = DSP market ~$6.35B; x Broadcom ~30% (100% - Marvell 62.5% (Stifel's unnamed chip type read as optical DSPs, id 80) - others ~7.5%) = $1.91B. TrendForce's newer 2026-11-02 release implies ~$47.8B for 2026 (2027 $84.1B / 1.76, src 161); the lower LightCounting reading is booked under the moderately conservative base case and the TrendForce reading is sized as an alternative. Was $26B (TrendForce April, id 78), overtaken by both. Lasers: Lumentum Components over the four quarters that match Broadcom's FY26 (Dec 2025 - Sep 2026) = 443.7 + 533.3 + 649.4 + 754.2 = $2,380.6M (src 164, src 163; was the single Jun-2026 quarter x 4); x 75% datacom lasers (judgment: the rest is telecom and pump lasers, which led its Sep quarter) = $1,785M; / ~55% Lumentum share (id 83) = datacom laser market ~$3.25B; x Broadcom ~18% blended (EML ~8.5% [TrendForce via Aetrix: Lumentum + Broadcom + Mitsubishi ~72% of EML, id 78, less Lumentum ~55%, id 83, split with Mitsubishi]; CW ~25% and VCSEL ~30% are the set's judgment, low confidence: no source gives Broadcom's CW or VCSEL share, Aetrix/TrendForce only lists Broadcom among the CW-DFB leaders whose top four hold ~74% of capacity, id 78, and the CEO claims 'a fairly substantial share', id 76) = $0.58B (CW and VCSEL at the EML ~8.5% instead: lasers $0.28B, optics share 12.68%, sized as an optics_share alternative). FY26 AI networking from the quarter xpu_shares on the booked Q4 FY26: 8,400 x (1 - 0.6667) + 10,800 x (1 - 0.61) + 16,700 x (1 - 0.73) + 21,496 x (1 - 0.734) = 2,799.7 + 4,212.0 + 4,509.0 + 5,717.9 = 17,238.7. Share = 2,490.1 / 17,238.7 = 14.44%, booked for every FY26 quarter including Q4 (no source gives optics by quarter). Value-neutral by itself: optics stays at the 72% networking margin (no cited split); it sizes the Marvell-Lumentum effect. FY27-FY29 held at the FY26 level (owner card 2026-11-09 'Hold both flat'): no source sizes a rising share; LightCounting expects linear-drive optics to cut DSP sales (id 84) and TrendForce has CPO moving value from pluggables into switches (src 161), against lasers 'far surpassing supply' (id 76). Was 11.35% (2026-11-17, $26B transceivers and one Lumentum quarter x 4), 10.4% before.
drivers.why: Sizes the exposure to the combined Marvell-Lumentum: FY28 optics ~$6.2B (Q4 FY28 run-rate ~$7.9B on the booked AI revenue).
drivers.variant: TrendForce's 2026-11-02 reading (2026 transceivers ~$47.8B, src 161): 17.95% of networking, the deal effect x1.24.

drivers.label: Net optics revenue lost to the combined Marvell-Lumentum after the close (probability-weighted)
drivers.source: Deal: 4.5 MRVL per LITE, close expected 1H CY2028, 'pre-validated optical solutions' (lasers, transceivers, OCS, InP) (id 75); Broadcom today the only full optical path to a hyperscaler (id 82); Lumentum NPO/CPO win backed by >$5B commitments (id 85). Reverse case: Stifel, module makers may switch away from Marvell DSPs after the deal (id 80); Innolight/Eoptolink already on Broadcom's Sian2 DSP (id 81); channel conflict with Lumentum's Cloud Light modules (id 82). Close probability 0.75 (MRVL round 2026-11-02, id 86).
drivers.derivation: Run-rate if the deal closes: gross -10% of Broadcom optics revenue (hyperscaler-specified bundles of Marvell DSP + Lumentum lasers/modules, and CPO/NPO engines where Lumentum already holds a >$5B win (Lumentum Q1 FY27 release, src 118); judgment) offset by +5% (module makers and Lumentum's laser customers that compete with Cloud Light moving DSP and laser orders to Broadcom, the only other merchant DSP and a CW/EML leader with tripling capacity; sized from the MRVL round's Stifel DSP dis-synergy, ~$0.45B of Marvell DSP revenue at FY28-29 scale, about two-thirds to Broadcom = ~$0.3B, ~5% of Broadcom optics): net -5%. Timing: expected close ~2028-04-01 (middle of 1H CY2028); 25% of run-rate in Q3 FY28, 50% Q4 FY28, 75% FY29, 100% from FY30 (integration and design cycles). Probability 0.75. Quarters = 0.75 x 5% x ramp. Not cut for landing after the horizon; FY29+ in the adjustment 'Marvell-Lumentum optics effect after the NTM year'. FY2029 ramp 62.5% / 70% / 80% / 87.5% of run-rate (avg 75%), x 0.75 x 5%.
drivers.why: Kilian 2026-11-02 card 'Yes, size it in AVGO'.
drivers.variant: Downside: gross -20%, no reverse gain (net -20%), price -6%: ~-$4.4/share. Upside: reverse case wins (net +5%, no price cut): ~+$0.6/share.

drivers.label: AI/data-center revenue lost to US data-center moratoria (expected share)
drivers.source: Scenario weights and no redirect: owner decision card 2026-11-05 ('Book it with spread at 30%'; thread 'Size moratorium risk for AVGO and NVDA'); proposal driver_models/AVGO/moratorium_proposal_avgo_nvda.md; sources [src 89, 90, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97, 98, 99, 100, 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107, 109, 110, 111, 112, 116, 117].
drivers.derivation: Expected share of Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue (ai_rev: XPUs and AI networking) lost to US data-center moratoria. Haircut = US deployment share x affected-state share x early-stage share x share of the window delayed; no redirect (owner decision card 2026-11-05). US share 0.693 = NVIDIA FY2026 revenue billed in the United States $149,617M / $215,938M [src 93] (NVIDIA's 10-K revenue by region, billing location, borrowed for AVGO, which discloses no deployment split: flagged). State shares, capacity basis for every state (owner 2026-11-05: 'everything should be on a capacity basis'): dcmap.us pipeline GW (under construction + planned, the stock the early-stage haircut acts on; operating capacity excluded), 'Data updated Oct 2026', read 2026-11-05 [src 116]; US pipeline 345.9 GW = 69.6 under construction + 276.3 planned [src 116, 117]. Texas 19.5 + 73.6 = 93.1 GW = 0.2692. PJM states VA 8.3+23.3 = 31.6, PA 8.1+15 = 23.1, OH 3.8+13.8 = 17.6, IL 1.9+8.7 = 10.6, NJ 0.340+0.295 = 0.635, MD 0.444+1.1 = 1.544, half of IN (4.1+4.6)/2 = 4.35: 89.429 GW = 0.2585 (Texas + PJM 0.5277). Georgia 1.2+18.6 = 19.8 GW = 0.0572, spread scenario only (weight 0.30, like PJM; owner card 2026-11-05 'Georgia in spread scenario'): ABC News projected Bottoms to win (2026-11-03 [src 109]) and said 'We need to pause' [src 110]; Bloomberg: called for a moratorium on new construction [src 107]; no scope or duration given. New York 0.382+5.7 = 6.082 GW = 0.0176. Caveat (flagged): dcmap's figures are 'reported or announced' and rounded, and a project's figure may be IT load, utility service or whole-campus power. Cross-checks: SemiAnalysis via Bloomberg: Texas 'nearly 30%' of US capacity coming online in 2028 [src 107]; BNEF ~20% of the US pipeline [src 90]; UBS via Finimize (2026-11-04): 'about 30% of expected 2028 capacity additions at risk' [src 111], not booked separately. Replaces this morning's mixed basis (Texas 0.29 capacity, others Cleanview building counts). Early stage 0.70 (BNEF via Utility Dive: 'more than 70%' of ~50 GW of Texas projects early stage [src 90]). Texas measures: ERCOT 'has paused the energization of new Large Load data centers' not yet connected 'until the completion of the verification and audit and community impact review', with the verification and community-impact reports to be filed with the PUCT by 2026-12-10 and a 'TBD impact' on the Batch Zero timeline [src 97, 96], after the Governor's directive to the PUCT and ERCOT to audit all data centers in the interconnection process before any more advance [src 98]; TCEQ data-center permits paused 'until ERCOT completes its review' (letter 2026-09-21) [src 99]. None of these sets a duration. Timing (gate 2026-11-05, same evidence and timing as the NVDA round): no Texas source sets an end date; the pause ends with the 2026-12-10 reports or, in the Texas-pause scenario, when the Legislature acts: Hinojosa called for a moratorium 'until a legislative session that puts Texans first' / until the legislature 'can adopt statewide regulations' [src 101, 102]; the 90th regular session runs 2027-01-12 to 2027-05-31 [src 103, 104]. So a 10-month pause, 2026-08-03 to 2027-05-31 (estimate, low confidence). An early-stage site takes about 12 months from construction start to operation at the fast end (Stargate Abilene buildings 1-2 operational 12 months after construction began [src 106]; Epoch AI: 1 to 3.6 years to 1 GW [src 105]), so the pause first removes installed accelerators about 2027-08 and pushes those projects out by its length: calendar Aug 2027-May 2028, window share 1.0 (estimate). The PJM spread is assumed on the same timing (estimate: no PJM state has a pause in force). Texas/PJM part = 0.693 x 0.70 x 1.0 x (0.45 x 0.2692 + 0.30 x 0.5277) = 0.13555 of AI revenue in Aug 2027-May 2028, 0 after. Georgia part (spread scenario) = 0.693 x 0.70 x 0.30 x 0.0572 = 0.00833 in Jan-Oct 2028: estimate, pause from mid-January 2027, when Georgia's governor-elect is installed at the next session of the General Assembly (Ga. Const. Art. V, Sec. I, Para. II [src 112]), which meets on the second Monday in January, 2027-01-11 (Art. III, Sec. IV, Para. I(a) [src 120]), for the same 10 months assumed for Texas (no Georgia duration given), plus ~12 months to build [src 105, 106]. New York EO 62 [src 100] in every scenario: 0.693 x 0.70 x 0.0176 = 0.00853 from Jul 2027 on (2026-07-14 plus ~12 months to build). Quarter value = mean of its calendar months; years (FY2026/FY2027/FY2028) weighted by the booked ai_rev quarters (after the SemiAnalysis cut): 0.00000/0.05094/0.08466 (gate 3 fix 2026-11-18: re-weighted on the booked quarters; was 0.03673/0.09454 on the 2026-11-10 even split; quarter values unchanged); FY2029 0.00854. Delayed revenue that returns after a pause is not added back; no multiple change. Was (round 2026-11-04): Texas 0.1721 and PJM 0.3767 by Cleanview building count, New York 0.0106, no Georgia; years 0.0/0.03614/0.0672. | Update 2026-11-13: quarters unchanged (shared gross haircut); the build now applies (1 - hs_self_funded 0.387) x dc_mor (Kilian 2026-11-16 11:11Z: revenue from self-funding hyperscalers left untouched).
drivers.why: Texas, New York and possible PJM-state and Georgia pauses delay early-stage US data centers that the accelerators would be installed in during the horizon window.

Alternatives sized: Google $30B (0.42), Mizuho's $42B Anthropic 2027 (0.445). FY2028-29: the set's FY2028 ai_rev build 17.0 GW x $11.5B = 195,500 (Anthropic 8.5 GW, OpenAI 3.5 GW, others 5.0 GW); at most the 'others' 5.0 GW (Google, Meta and the rest) are self-funded: 57.5 / 195.5 = 0.294 (upper bound for the self-funded share; FY2029 holds FY2028's run-rate, so its mix). [src 38, 48]

drivers.derivation: By fiscal year: FY2028 0.294, FY2029 0.292, default 0.387 (dc_mor is zero before the haircut window, so reported quarters are unaffected). ESTIMATE from the AVGO set's own FY2027 AI revenue build (ai_rev, rebuild 2026-11-09, Q3 FY26 call ids 37, 38): Google own TPUs $34.2B (incl. networking) + Meta 1.0 GW x $11.5B = $45.7B of $118.15B = 0.387 self-funded; Anthropic 5.0 GW ($57.5B) and OpenAI 1.3 GW ($14.95B) are exposed (externally financed; Broadcom's 2026-10-27 8-K rack-lease backstop). Alternatives sized: Google $30B (0.42), Mizuho's $42B Anthropic 2027 (0.445). FY2028-29: the set's FY2028 ai_rev build 17.0 GW x $11.5B = 195,500 (Anthropic 8.5 GW, OpenAI 3.5 GW, others 5.0 GW); at most the 'others' 5.0 GW (Google, Meta and the rest) are self-funded: 57.5 / 195.5 = 0.294 (upper bound for the self-funded share; FY2029 = others 5.0 GW x $11.5B = 57.5B / FY29 AI revenue 197.11B = 0.292 (round 2026-11-16 mix; the 11-17 HBM pass-through scales TPU and non-TPU XPU revenue alike, so the share is left as booked), so its mix). Applied as (1 - hs_self_funded) x dc_mor wherever the build used dc_mor; dc_mor's quarters stay the shared gross values.

quarters.note: Segment operating income = Broadcom non-GAAP operating income (before SBC, acquired-intangible amortization and restructuring); corporate_ebit = -SBC, so EBIT is non-GAAP after SBC, the Zacks basis of the peer table. Constants: nonai_margin 55% for FY25-26 (rebuilt 2026-11-09 from the non-AI gross margin and cost base; was 52.5%), rebuilt 2026-11-17 for FY27-29 (55.1-57.2%); sbc per quarter (actuals XBRL ShareBasedCompensation; forecasts below). Rebuild 2026-10-30 (Kilian 'yes on mix the three new ones'): AI margin = XPU share x XPU margin + networking share x net_margin (72%, constant); non_ai_rev, sw_margin and sbc are constants. Update 2026-11-02 (Marvell-Lumentum): optics = ai_rev x (1 - xpu_share) x optics_share inside AI networking; the combined rival's net share loss and price cut come off optics revenue and EBIT (share loss at the 72% networking margin, price cut in full). FY2029 constants (rebuilt 2026-11-17): nonai_margin 57.0/56.0/55.9/57.2%, sbc 2,450, non_ai_rev 4,769.5/4,426.4/4,410.0/4,829.0 (+3.2% a year on FY28, judgment), sw_margin 82.9-82.4% (94% less $919M opex a quarter, judgment), net_margin 72% (held, no source; carded 2026-11-18).

adjustments.name: Marvell-Lumentum optics effect after the NTM year (FY29 ramp to run-rate, probability-weighted)
adjustments.note: Driven: the run-rate optics EBIT loss if the deal closes, R = Q4 FY28 optics run-rate 7,906.0 (booked Q4 FY28 ai_rev 58,594.4 after the SemiAnalysis cut x (1 - xpu_share 0.7664) x optics_share 0.1444 x 4; rebuilt 2026-11-18 on the rebuilt optics share, was 6,214 at 0.1135) x p 0.75 x (5% x 72% + 3% x 95%) x (1 - 16% tax) = 321.3 $M a year. FY28 (the horizon NTM year) already carries 0.1875 of R through the drivers; the P/E capitalises that level. The rest steps in at 75% in FY29 (+0.5625 R, one year after the horizon) and 100% from FY30 (+0.25 R, two years after), each capitalised at the booked horizon P/E 19.25x (own 19.81x x growth term 0.9719) and discounted at AVGO's cost of equity 13.56% (rf 4.24% + premium 9.32% at beta 1.91, priors 2026-11-02). Effects after the horizon are counted in full, discounted only for time and the 0.75 close probability (Kilian 2026-11-02). Value = -R x (0.5625 x 19.25 / 1.1356 + 0.25 x 19.25 / 1.1356^2) = -321.3 x 13.267 = -4,262.2.

base.story: FY27 AI $118.2B (7.3 GW x $11.5B + Google TPUs), FY28 AI $195.5B (17 GW x $11.5B) before the owner-picked SemiAnalysis cut, $185.1B booked after it, XPU margin 58.75% from FY27, software ~84% margin; P/E on the horizon NTM (= FY28) EPS after SBC.

downside.story: AI air pocket: lab financing or power slips; AI revenue 35% below the base path in every forecast quarter (FY27 ~$75-80B run-rate exit, FY28 ~$127B vs $195.5B; base round bear FY28 flat at $115B), XPU margin -3pt (AI margin ~-2.5pt at a 73% XPU share) on opex deleverage, P/E -4 turns. The downside customer-financing loss is in the unconditional adjustment, not in this delta.

upside.story: Management's line of sight: FY28 AI ~$225-230B (all 20 GW), FY27 ~$120B+; XPU margin -0.7pt (AI ~-0.5pt) on rack mix; P/E +2 turns.

inputs_detail.derivation: Rasgon (Bernstein) on the Q3 FY26 call: 'between $11 and $12 billion per gigawatt' (id 47; he divides management's outlook by customer GW); midpoint $11.5B per GW, owner card 2026-11-10 ('$11.5B (Rasgon midpoint)'). Cross-checks: (1) Mizuho (id 48) puts Broadcom's Anthropic AI revenue at $21B for 2026 and $42B for 2027 and, separately, the Anthropic deal at ~3.5 GW from 2027; Mizuho gives no per-GW price, so a per-GW figure is the set's division: $12.0B on 3.5 GW, $8.4B on the 5 GW Tan now cites for 2027 (ids 37, 38), ~$21B on 2026's 1 GW. (2) Chip content (estimate, low confidence): TPU-only price ~$9.3-10.1k = XPU revenue per Broadcom TPU unit ~$15.56k (Q4 FY26 build, driver ai_rev) x Google TPU's 60-65% of Broadcom's 2026 CoWoS pre-orders (36Kr packaging split, src 124; using the wafer split as the revenue split is the set's reading), x ~840-920k chips per GW (Google's 9,216-chip Ironwood pod 'roughly 10 megawatts under full load', src 132, = ~922k chips per GW; ~838k with ~10% facility overhead, estimate), plus networking at 0.37x XPU revenue (Q3 FY26 filed ratio): 838k x $9.34k x 1.37 = $10.7B to 922k x $10.11k x 1.37 = $12.8B per GW; both ends are sized as alternatives. Tan's / Kawwas's '$20 to $30 billion per gigawatt' is system content: Broadcom's 10-Q (Item 2, MD&A; id 32): 'In June 2026, we launched the AI XPV platform with an initial tranche of $35 billion led by a financial partner to facilitate the deployment of more than 1 gigawatt of compute infrastructure for our customer' (also on the Q3 FY26 call, ids 37, 38; R17 id 29), and Reuters on Anthropic's prospectus: 'about $161.2bn of Broadcom-related equipment lease obligations that are largely non-cancellable' (src 140), with a five-year TPU lease (Reuters via The Star, src 141); no filing shows rack value in Broadcom revenue, so it is not used as in-year revenue. Broadcom's purchase commitments are not used as an AI revenue check: they rose from $235M (Q3 FY25 10-Q, src 34) to ~$128.1B (Q2 FY26 10-Q, FY27 $55,214M + FY28 $72,870M, src 33), the quarter of Anthropic's March 2026 lease, so they are mostly rack purchases.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 call: 'in 2028 we have clear line of sight to deliver another, an incremental, 10 gigawatts'; Anthropic 'on track to become our largest XPU customer in 2027 and sustain that in 2028'. Support: Reuters reports Anthropic's Q3 revenue at $16.8B (+45% q/q) and profitable on an adjusted basis (src 51; the S-1/A figures could not be read on the rendered filing, so they are not used); about $161.2B of Broadcom-related equipment lease obligations, 'non-cancellable by either party except in the case of a default' (Reuters on the prospectus, src 140), on a five-year TPU lease (Reuters, src 141); IPO discussed at ~$1.5T (Reuters, 2026-10-15, id 51); financing in place ($35B XPV tranche, $60B package syndicating). Gross margin ~70%: Q4 FY23 segment gross margin ~70% when non-AI was ~$5.8B of $7.3B (CFO, src 129); non-AI prices have been held (no cut named on any call since). Operating expenses ~$0.62B a quarter: the segment's $822M in Q4 FY23 ('stable year-on-year') less ~25% for the AI R&D already in it (AI ~20% of Q4 FY23 segment revenue, judgment); every increase since (to $1.1B in Q4 FY25 and $1.2B in Q3 FY26) is named as AI R&D ('increased investment in R&D for leading-edge AI semiconductors', src 130; Q3 FY26 'reflected investments in R&D', ids 37, 38). That argues WSTS's 2027 rate is not too high for the market. Was 8,750 (gate 2026-11-17: the guide booked without a declaration). FY27-FY29 rebuilt 2026-11-17 (carry-forward fix): revenue follows VMware's recurring base, which is the installed workloads times the price per workload. (1) Today: ARR +15% y/y at Q3 FY26 ('we sustained ARR growth of 15% year-on-year', id 38; +17% at Q2 FY26, id 88) and management expected the faster VMware growth 'to continue' (Q2 FY26 call, June 2026, id 88). That growth is the first Broadcom-era repricing onto VCF: in CloudBolt's January 2026 survey 14% of customers saw increases above 100%, 12% 50-99%, 33% 24-49% and 31% below 25% (via Petri, https://petri.com/vmware-pricing-fears-enterprise-virtualization-shift/). (2) Workloads: Gartner expects 'More than a third of workloads currently running under VMware will run on another platform by 2028' (The Register, 2025-09-11, https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/11/gartner_vmware_migration_advice/): 35% lost over Sep 2025-Dec 2028 = -12.4% a year; CloudBolt: '86% of organizations report actively reducing their VMware footprint'. judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Does the TPU v9 memory step cut AVGO's XPU margin in FY28-29?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: Custom XPU operating margin (before SBC) is booked at 55.90% FY27 / 51.06% FY28 / 46.30% FY29 since the owner's pick 2026-11-16 ('v9 HBM4, half of FY28'). FY27 has every XPU at the full TPU 8i memory (HBM) step, from the set's own formula (288 GB HBM3e x $12.2/GB x 1.1 = 23.4% of XPU revenue, resold at ~10% margin vs ~69.5% on the rest, +0.3pt opex leverage). FY27 rests on the Q3 FY26 call (Broadcom ships TPU 8i; Anthropic's 2027 5 GW are 8i). For FY28-29 the evidence points lower but does not size it: JPMorgan (via a relay page) says TPU v9 ramps in volume in 2028 with four compute dies and 16 HBM stacks; Silicon Analysts expects HBM4 at ~$36/GB for 2027 supply (vs ~$12.2 for HBM3e in 2026). No source gives v9's memory capacity, its price per chip, or what share of FY28 TPUs it is. The builds below assume 36 GB HBM4 stacks (576 GB) and that v9's non-memory value is twice 8i's for twice the compute dies (the set's estimate). One caveat favors the booked level: revenue per GW is held at $11.5B, so pricier memory passed through would also raise revenue, which these builds do not add. CEO Hock Tan's 'sustain operating margin even as mix of products dilutes the gross margin' is consolidated. Update 2026-11-17: the owner-picked SemiAnalysis reading (volume net of dc_mor) leaves xpu_margin on this path.

options.reasoning: Holds the FY27 memory share; if v9 doubles both memory and compute content, the share is unchanged (sized: no change).

options.label: v9 at HBM4, half of FY28
options.reasoning: v9 ramps during 2028, so half of FY28 TPU revenue and all of FY29 carry 576 GB at $36.11/GB; memory 47% of TPU revenue, TPU margin 41.6%.

options.label: v9 at HBM4, all of FY28
options.reasoning: Same build with every FY28-29 TPU on v9: TPU margin 41.6%, blended XPU ~46%.

options.label: v9 576 GB, 8i compute value
options.reasoning: The gate's build: 576 GB at today's $12.2/GB on 8i's non-memory value; memory 38%, TPU margin 47.3% in FY28-29.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.item: SemiAnalysis Nov 13 ASIC revenue cut (HBM pass-through)
judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: How to read SemiAnalysis's 11% cut to Broadcom ASIC revenue?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: SemiAnalysis's Nov 13 Accelerator & HBM Model update (paywalled; read through two relays) cuts Broadcom's cumulative 2026-30 ASIC revenue by 11%, 'mainly due to average selling price adjustments from lower HBM costs rather than large-scale shipment reductions' (Tiger relay) and 'largely driven by price deflation rather than volume collapse', with Broadcom 'largely insulated' (456X relay). Our set builds AI revenue as customer GW x $11.5B per GW, with HBM resold at ~10% margin inside XPU revenue. The owner picked 'Volume net of moratorium' (card 2026-11-17 9:38 AM ET): the set books it as a volume cut on all AI revenue (XPUs and networking) net of the moratorium overlap, ai_rev x 0.89 / (1 - (1 - hs_self_funded) x dc_mor) in FY27-FY29, with Q1 FY27 (two-thirds calendar 2026, which SemiAnalysis left 'essentially unchanged') taking a third of it; xpu_share and xpu_margin are unchanged. This reads against the relays' price-led wording, by the owner's choice. It is a call because the relays give no per-year split and no price/volume split, and the primary note cannot be read.

options.label: HBM pass-through
options.reasoning: Both relays say the Broadcom cut is mainly lower HBM prices, not fewer chips; HBM is resold at a thin margin, so lower HBM prices cut revenue much more than profit (XPU EBIT -2% for -11% XPU revenue). GW stay on the company's Q3 FY26 call figures, and dc_mor keeps the delay risk.

options.label: Volume reading, all AI revenue x 0.89
options.reasoning: Treats the 11% as fewer deployments: every AI dollar (XPUs and networking) falls 11% at today's margins. This reads against both relays' wording and counts SemiAnalysis's 5.8 GW midterm delay on top of our own moratorium haircut, so it is the upper bound of the cut.

options.label: Volume, per-year SA profile
options.reasoning: Volume reading with the cut timed like SemiAnalysis's own spend cuts (2027 -19%, 2028 -28%, 2029 -41%), scaled to Broadcom's 11% over 2026-30 with FY26 already reported: FY27 -6.7%, FY28 -9.9%, FY29 -14.5%. Timed as pass-through instead: 435.23 (+5.38%).

options.label: Volume, net of moratorium overlap (booked, owner pick)
options.reasoning: Same volume reading, but the moratorium haircut already in the set counts toward the 11%, so the 5.8 GW delay is not taken twice. Half price, half volume lands at the same place (-3.92%).

options.label: No change (11-16 set)
options.reasoning: Keeps $11.5B per GW from Rasgon and our own HBM prices (Silicon Analysts), on the view that a relay of a paywalled model is not enough to move our independent build.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Which FCF yield for AVGO's new 40% FCF leg?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: Your 11-17 rule adds a FCF yield leg at 40% next to P/E 60% for tech names whose forward FCF margin stays above 2% (AVGO's minimum is 43%). The rule says to use the peers' median FCF yield, but on 10-30 you set AVGO's P/E at its own 19.81x because faster-growing peers skew the median. The set books the same footing for the FCF leg: AVGO's own forward FCF yield = trailing FCF / Zacks EPS conversion (0.9408) / own NTM P/E 19.81x = 4.75%, / growth factor 0.9719 = 4.887%. The leg moves the research target (12m) from 416.43 (P/E only) to 412.79 (-0.87%). Peer-based yields would move it more; the peer exit rule now puts AVGO and the peers on one basis (TTM FCF / GAAP net income).

options.label: Own forward yield 4.887% (booked)
options.reasoning: Same basis as your own-P/E decision: AVGO's own cash conversion of its earnings, priced at its own multiple. The leg then values the gap between our forecast FCF and our forecast EPS rather than a peer re-rating.

options.label: Peer exit rule 4.607%
options.reasoning: The standard exit rule on the peers' NTM-converted FCF yields (NVDA 6.10%, AMD 2.42%, MRVL 2.46%, CRDO 4.60%, ALAB 1.60%; median 2.46%) pulled 80% of the way toward AVGO's own yield on the same basis (TTM FCF / GAAP net income 1.0297 over 19.81x = 5.198%), / 0.9719. It follows the rule's peer wording but uses the skewed median you rejected for P/E.

options.label: Plain peer median 2.535%
options.reasoning: The rule's literal peer median: AVGO priced like AMD, MRVL and ALAB, which grow faster and trade at 27-47x. It would more than undo the own-P/E decision on 40% of the value.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: It keeps the leg on the same footing as your own-P/E choice and is the moderately conservative option. Sizes re-shown 2026-11-18 off base 412.79 (gate round 3 set): Peer exit rule 4.607% 422.75 (+2.41%); Plain peer median 2.535% 564.69 (+36.80%).

disagreements.topic: FY28 AI semiconductor revenue anchor ($175-184B) vs the house capex input and the 10-Q purchase commitments
disagreements.positions: agent_1 $180B; agent_2 $180B (band $166-185B); agent_3 $175B; agent_4 $184B (230 x 0.8); agent_5 $177B (mean of $140.9B / $159.3B / $230B). Management: 'line of sight ... to again double to $230 billion. Here again, we have secured the supply'.
disagreements.resolution: Keep $180B as the base; the agents' range is consistent with both inputs, but it is not the conservative end. Mechanical anchors: constant share of house base capex 0.0625 x $2,255B = $141B; purchase commitments FY28/FY27 72,952/52,674 = 1.385 x $115B = $159B (AI-only) or $166B (semis-only, agent 2). $180B is 8.0% of 2028 base capex vs 6.2% in 2027, i.e. a +1.8pt share gain carried by the GW roadmap (Anthropic +5 GW in 2027 and +10 GW in 2028; OpenAI 1.3 GW and >5 GW). Two points weaken the 'commitments are still filling in' argument: the FY28 bucket was flat over the quarter ($72,870M at 2026-05-03 vs $72,952M at 2026-08-02) while FY27 fell ($55,214M -> $52,674M). The house file (as of 2026-10-05) is the capex base; no newer company capex guide exists, so no deviation from it. $230B needs a 10.2% share of base capex or the house high case (7.3%) and stays the bull case; the house low case (2028 $1,265B < 2027 $1,390B) mechanically gives 115 x 1,265/1,390 = $104.7B (estimate); the bear uses ~$110B, a judgment between that and the $115B FY27 guide.
disagreements.evidence: Q3 call (Webull/Benzinga transcript, opened): '$115 billion', '$230 billion', 'Here again, we have secured the supply to meet this outlook', GW figures. 10-Q R53 (opened): FY27 $52,674M, FY28 $72,952M, total $126,821M. Q2 10-Q R52 (opened): $55,214M / $72,870M / $128,110M. FY25 10-Q R59 (opened): total commitments a year earlier $235M. House capex file table 1: 2027 1,390/1,841/2,434, 2028 1,265/2,255/3,160.

comps_review.premium_discount_judgment: A ~26% discount to the 25.8x median is accepted as persistent, but only because it is the discount the market applies today on the same basis, not because a re-rating is forecast: 19x equals AVGO's own 19.46x. Supporting facts that last through Oct-2027: (1) the mega-cap AI-silicon cohort is priced below the median on the same CY2027 basis today (NVDA 15.3x with +70% next-year EPS growth, TSM 21.8x, AVGO 19.5x), so the discount is observed, not assumed; (2) at the horizon the NTM year is FY28, with base EPS growth +24% ($24.06 vs $19.39) against a peer median 'EPS next Y' of +49.9% (Finviz; mixed fiscal years, indicative only); growth-matched peers (TSM +31%, ADI +29%, ANET +28%) trade 21.8-40.9x, so part of the discount rests on (3) and (4); (3) concentration: six XPU customers, 'four of them are just simply going to be huge' (Q3 call); (4) the 10-Q Backstop (~$29B max) and $42B note facility to one customer, with further XPV tranches unsized. A multiple above today's 19.5x would need evidence of re-rating; a multiple below NVDA's 15.3x would need an earnings stall, which belongs in the bear case. No agent claims a premium; agent 3's 18x is inside the range but its extra discount below AVGO's own multiple is not separately evidenced.

round1_to_round2.convergence_verdict: Partly anchoring, partly independent. Anchored on my round-1 file: four of five agents moved FY28 AI to within $4B of my $180B (from 175-205), four adopted my 23.7x peer median including my wrong fiscal-year labels for CSCO and COHR (agents 3 and 5 copied 'FY27 to Jul-2027' / 'FY27 to Jun-2027' verbatim; agents 1 and 4 wrote '~CY2027 for every peer'), three use exactly my 19x, and all five restate the thesis break as ~13-14x the same $19.39 consensus. Independent: agent 2 re-derived the peer basis and found my labelling error (verified, see comps_review); agents 4 and 5 replaced my unsourced 10.5% with a sourced CAPM rate; agent 2 added the Q2 10-Q commitment table; every agent rebuilt FY28 EPS bottom-up with its own segment or margin-slope model. The round-2 mean FV ($405) landed below my round-1 $420, not on it, mostly because of the discount rate. So the tighter FV spread (s.d. $21.5 -> $15.5) overstates independent agreement: the FY28 AI input and the peer median are effectively one source (my round-1 file), and the 10% dispersion floor in conviction.py remains the right treatment.

My reconciled fair value is $400 (19x FY28 EPS ~$24.1 blended with a $293 DCF), +6% vs $377.32, with a ladder median ~$388 and thesis break $260. Agent 2 caught a round-1 error of mine that four agents had copied: CSCO, COHR and CRDO are on fiscal 2028 in Finviz, so the CY2027 peer median is 25.8x, not 23.7x; AVGO's 19.5x is a persistent mega-cap AI-silicon discount, and the multiple used (19x) is unchanged. options.label: Keep 58.75% (booked)
